technology.value: 12 m diameter acrylic vessel holding 1000 t of heavy water (D2O), viewed by 9600 photomultiplier tubes on a geodesic support structure, submerged in ordinary water inside a 2039 m deep rock cavity
technology.quote: 1000 tonnes of heavy water (D2O) ... 12 meter diameter acrylic vessel ... 9600 photomultiplier tubes mounted on a geodesic support structure

placements.quote: Nov 1999 -- Production data taking begins ... Nov 2006 -- End of datataking for 3rd phase
placements.note: Placed at site:snolab-underground-lab (owned by the facilities workstream), the original SNO cavern that SNOLAB later expanded around; not created here.

intervals.label: phase 1: pure D2O
intervals.quote: Nov 1999 -- Production data taking begins ... May 2001 -- Start of 2nd phase of data taking (salt fill)

intervals.label: phase 2: NaCl-doped D2O
intervals.quote: May 2001 -- Start of 2nd phase of data taking (salt fill)

intervals.label: phase 3: NCD array
intervals.quote: Feb 2004 -- Start of 3rd phase of data taking (with NCD detectors) ... Nov 2006 -- End of datataking for 3rd phase

intervals.label: drained / decommissioned as SNO
intervals.quote: May 2007 -- D2O drained from acrylic vessel
intervals.note: The same acrylic vessel and cavern were subsequently refitted for SNO+ (experiment:sno-plus).

pmt_count.quote: 9600 photomultiplier tubes mounted on a geodesic support structure

description.value: An array of proportional counters strung through the heavy water in phase 3 to independently detect the neutral-current reaction via neutron capture
description.quote: Feb 2004 -- Start of 3rd phase of data taking (with NCD detectors)

summary.plain: A 12-metre acrylic ball full of heavy water, watched by 9,600 light sensors, sitting two kilometres underground in a Canadian mine.
summary.technical: Water-Cherenkov detector: 1000 t D2O in a 12 m diameter acrylic vessel viewed by 9600 PMTs, run in three configurations (pure D2O; NaCl-doped; D2O plus an NCD proportional-counter array) between 1999 and 2006.
